blocks.text: Consider a circuit in which a coil is connected in series with a battery, a switch and a rheostat as shown in Fig.17.18. If we move the rheostat quickly, the primary current through the coil will change. The magnetic flux through the coil will also change, which finally induces an emf in the coil itself.
The phenomenon, in which changing current induces an emf inside the coil itself, is called self-induction.
bold: The phenomenon, in which changing current induces an emf inside the coil itself, is called self-induction.

The self-inductance of the coil can also be defined as ratio of the emf to the rate of change of current in the same coil. The SI unit of self-inductance L is Vs A⁻¹ having dimensions [ML²T⁻²A⁻²].

Example 17.8
A coil has an inductance reactance of 160 Ω at a frequency of 50 Hz. Calculate self-inductance of the coil.
Solution
Induced reaction X_L = 160 Ω, Frequency f = 59 Hz
We know that; X_L = 2πfL
or L = X_L/2πf
